---
title: "Features"
subtitle: "Most of Emaki explains itself once it is open. This is the tour; the shortcuts are at the foot."
---

## Sessions and projects {.i-scroll}

The sidebar lists every project, pinned ones above the rest, with headings at
the foot for hidden projects and temporary folders. **All Sessions** unfolds
each project in place, every session dated and ordered by when it last did
something, archived projects in their own section.

Select sessions or projects together ([⌘]{.kbd}-click, [⇧]{.kbd}-click, a
dragged rectangle or [⌘A]{.kbd}), then archive them now, delete them, or
open them in Finder. Archive checks Emaki's own copy first; Delete moves
every copy to the Trash. Nothing in a project's own folder is touched.

A session Claude Code has deleted stays listed, marked *kept*. Renaming a
session renames it for Claude Code too, and each one keeps its own draft.
Tabs group into per-project pills, drag to reorder, and answer to
[⌘1]{.kbd} to [⌘9]{.kbd}.

## Search {.i-search}

[⌘K]{.kbd} searches every session on the machine. The index holds one entry
per *item*, a prompt, a reply's paragraph, a thought, a tool call, so a hit
lands on the thing you remembered rather than the file it was in. Live and
kept sessions are searched together.

[⌘F]{.kbd} finds inside the conversation you are reading; [⌘G]{.kbd} and
[⌘⇧G]{.kbd} step through the hits.

## Conversation {.i-book-open}

Prompts, replies, tool calls, thoughts and subagents, laid out like the
Claude app. Prompts sit in a bubble with a tail, tool badges are coloured by
kind, and tool calls, thoughts and rows open and close in motion. Code
blocks are coloured, carry a copy button and scroll sideways instead of
wrapping.

**Explain** puts one plain sentence on an opaque tool call, asked of the
session's own agent: Haiku for Claude Code, Codex's light model for Codex.
The **outline** ([⌘⇧O]{.kbd}) is a short label per prompt; click one to
jump there. An agent's progress notes show as part of the reply, as in the
terminal, and a running command says what it is for.

## Composer {.i-inbox}

Type to reply. A session running in a terminal gets the message through
Claude Code's inbox; a finished one resumes under Emaki.

- Attach files by paste, drop or the **+** button.
- `@` picks a file or folder from the project; a path that exists takes the
  accent colour. `/` lists the folder's slash commands.
- Spelling and grammar are checked as you type (English US and UK; Spanish,
  French and German spelling on a Mac), with corrections, *Learn Spelling*
  and *Ignore* on the right-click menu.
- Send with [⌘↩]{.kbd} or [↩]{.kbd}, your choice; [⇧↩]{.kbd} is always a new
  line. Drafts survive quitting.

## Dictation {.i-microphone}

On a Mac, press [⌘⇧D]{.kbd} or the microphone button and talk. A model you
download once in Settings, Dictate (Qwen3-ASR or Whisper) writes it down on
this machine, Chinese and English mixed in one sentence, and the words go in
at the caret. Nothing you say leaves the Mac. [Esc]{.kbd} cancels while it
listens.

- **Post-processing**, when it is on, hands the words to a small language
  model (Qwen3.5, in three sizes) that removes hesitations, applies
  corrections ("100, no, 200"), mends grammar and makes lists, in any
  language, without translating. What it writes is taken only when it keeps
  to what was said.
- **Preferences** are your own instructions to that model, in plain words,
  which it follows over its own rules. **Terms** are names and words written
  exactly as you save them, capitals and all.
- The shortcut works in any app: the words are pasted where you type, your
  clipboard put back after, and a pill at the top of the screen shows it
  listening. Allow Accessibility from Settings, Dictate.
- Dictation can also start and stop on a modifier tapped alone, such as
  Right ⌘ or Fn. A history of what was said is kept on this Mac for as long
  as you choose, with a window to look back and copy.

## Agent control {.i-sparkles}

Mode, model and effort are pills under the composer, each in the agent's own
colours, each opening a list in place. [⇧Tab]{.kbd} steps the mode as it
does in the terminal. Approvals, questions and plans arrive as cards at the
conversation's end, and whatever else the agent asks that Emaki has no card
for comes up on the terminal card, so nothing waits unseen. A plan is shown
on its approval card and kept in the conversation.

Stop a turn from the window; the stopped message comes back to the composer
if the agent had not started on it. A Claude Code left running after its
terminal closed is named as such, with a button to stop it and continue
here. The row under the composer shows context left and rate limits, for
both agents.

## Terminal {.i-terminal}

The button at the top right opens a terminal beside the conversation: a
shell in the session's folder, or the session's own agent as it runs, drawn
whole and two-way. Shells open in tabs. Mouse selection copies on release,
mouse-aware programs take clicks and scrolls, and the Mac's terminal line
keys work ([⌘←]{.kbd}, [⌘→]{.kbd}, [⌘⌫]{.kbd}, [⇧↩]{.kbd}, [⌘K]{.kbd}).
[⌘⇧S]{.kbd} and [⌘⇧A]{.kbd} show and hide the panel's two sides.

## Files and editing {.i-tree-view}

The files panel ([⌘⇧E]{.kbd}) is a tree of the project with git's marks on
it, and it works like a file manager: drag in from Finder, drag rows to
move, cut, copy, duplicate, remove with [⌘⌫]{.kbd}, undo with [⌘Z]{.kbd}.
Click a file to open it in a pane beside the conversation:

| | |
|---|---|
| Code | line numbers, colours, a gutter mark per git change with a card to see or revert it |
| Markdown | as it reads or as written; a YAML header shows as a table of its fields |
| CSV | a grid with lettered columns, editable in place, each column its own colour |
| Parquet | a table with each column's type and the row count |
| Word | pages you can type in, style and format, saved with [⌘S]{.kbd} |
| PowerPoint, Excel | slides drawn as they look, cells with their number formats |
| PDF | sharp at any width, with search, selection, page previews and a table of contents |
| HTML | in the system's web view, scripts and all |
| Pictures | shown |

: {.table-keys tbl-colwidths="[26,74]"}

Unsaved changes are never lost without asking. Format on save covers ten
languages (R, Python, Rust, Go, C and C++, TypeScript, JavaScript, JSON,
Markdown, TOML) and is off until you turn it on.

## Git {.i-git-branch}

The **Changes** sheet commits the files you tick, discards several at once,
and has a History tab: browse commits, undo the last one, revert one. Push,
Pull and Fetch sit where the counts are. Branches are listed, created
([⌘⇧N]{.kbd}), switched, carrying your changes along or leaving them behind,
and published. When the remote refuses, a sheet says how to sign in.

## Agents {.i-bot}

The Agents page ([⌘E]{.kbd}) says which agents are installed and signed in,
and walks through installing one, a numbered step at a time for this
machine, with a shell beside the steps. GitHub is there too: install git,
sign in, and tell git who your commits are by.

## Settings {.i-settings}

[⌘,]{.kbd} opens nine pages: Appearance, Fonts, Composer, Dictate, New
sessions, Terminal, Files, Updates and About. Appearance follows the system
or pins light or dark, and the accent is one of six: terracotta, blue, green,
violet, teal or graphite. Eight chat faces and four monospace faces ship with
the app, all under the Open Font License, with one text size across the
conversation, the file editor and the terminal. New sessions sets each
agent's mode, model and effort to begin with.

## What it will not do {.i-shield}

::: {.checks}
- **No hooks, ever.**
- Nothing writes to a transcript. The JSONL file is the only source of truth, and Emaki reads it.
- Nothing Emaki does enters a session's context window.
- Nothing is typed into a terminal of yours, and no terminal app is asked for anything. Emaki runs its own, hidden.
- Copy first, render second. If rendering fails, the bytes are already safe.
:::

## Keyboard {.i-keyboard}

[⌘]{.kbd} on macOS, [Ctrl]{.kbd} elsewhere.

| | |
|---|---|
| [⌘K]{.kbd} | search every session |
| [⌘F]{.kbd} · [⌘G]{.kbd} · [⌘⇧G]{.kbd} | find in this conversation, next, previous |
| [⌘N]{.kbd} | new session |
| [⌘T]{.kbd} | new session in this project |
| [⌘O]{.kbd} | choose a folder |
| [⌘L]{.kbd} | sessions |
| [⌘E]{.kbd} | agents |
| [⌘,]{.kbd} | settings |
| [⌘B]{.kbd} | sidebar |
| [⌘⇧E]{.kbd} | files panel |
| [⌘⇧O]{.kbd} | outline |
| [⌘⇧S]{.kbd} · [⌘⇧A]{.kbd} | the terminal panel's shell, the agent's side |
| [⌘1]{.kbd} to [⌘9]{.kbd} | tabs |
| [⌘W]{.kbd} · [⌘⇧T]{.kbd} | close a tab, reopen the last |
| [⌘S]{.kbd} | save the file |
| [⌘↩]{.kbd} | send |
| [⌘⇧N]{.kbd} | new branch |
| [⌘⇧D]{.kbd} | dictate |
| [⌘R]{.kbd} | refresh |
| [Esc]{.kbd} | stop, or close what is open |

: {.table-keys tbl-colwidths="[38,62]"}

In the terminal, [⌘T]{.kbd} opens a tab, [⌘W]{.kbd} closes it and
[⌘K]{.kbd} clears the screen.
